text: {"standards":[{"code":"W.6.2","verdict":"partly","reason":"In Finalize the Explanatory Essay, students check thesis connection, transitions, and evidence, but they do not select or analyze new content, so the explanatory-writing skill is only partly practiced."},{"code":"W.6.4","verdict":"taught","reason":"The Clear, Consistent, Concise mini-lesson and the Finalize the Explanatory Essay style checklist have students fix terminology, redundancy, pronouns, and formal style for their audience."},{"code":"W.6.6","verdict":"partly","reason":"The Finalize activity only mentions that students may keyboard their final copy, with no instruction in using technology to publish, collaborate, or type sustained pages."},{"code":"W.6.8","verdict":"partly","reason":"The Finalize activity has students paraphrase and name page or source for evidence and include a source list, and a teacher note touches on credibility, but students do not gather or assess multiple sources in this lesson."},{"code":"W.6.9","verdict":"taught","reason":"In Finalize the Explanatory Essay, students add quotations or paraphrases from The Lightning Thief and tie each paragraph's evidence explicitly to the thesis."},{"code":"W.6.9.a","verdict":"partly","reason":"Only an optional extension asks students to compare a value in The Lightning Thief with a second text, so applying literary analysis to compare genres or approaches to themes is touched rather than taught."},{"code":"W.6.10","verdict":"taught","reason":"Students revise an extended essay over a class period and complete the final draft as homework, which is routine writing across a shorter and an extended time frame."}],"anchorText":{"verdict":"uses","reason":"The Lightning Thief is named as the text for the Finalize and Prepare Key Claims activities, with Percy's loyalty to Grover as the cited evidence, matching the Outline."}}
